The revision is complete in `task/`; nothing else was touched.

**Summary of the planted issues.** The matter is a self-funded ERISA plan (Halvorsen) whose TPA (Meridian, a subsidiary of carrier Continental) resists a consultant's request for claim-level data. The original ASA plants the clear violations — a consent right over sharing with consultants/auditors defined as "Competitors" (§ 9.4), a bar on disclosing rates to participants and referring providers (§ 9.5), 250-claim/once-a-year/view-only audit caps (§ 9.6), and transition/survival clauses that extend the restrictions to a successor TPA (§§ 9.8/12.5) — alongside the genuinely unsettled § 9.3 terms (paid custom extracts, 180 days from an open-ended acceptance, a "proprietary" decline right), a savings clause the TPA says cures everything, and an upstream Continental network-license clause (§ 4.3) that is the real source of the restriction. New in this iteration, and the main difficulty driver, is Meridian's own "standard CAA Data Access Amendment" offered with an October 30 fee-waiver deadline: it fixes the obvious problems (consent, 180 days, per-line pricing) while re-creating the restrictions in subtler forms — provider-key masking labelled as "de-identification" with named-provider data relegated back to a declinable custom extract, a notice-and-objection right that withholds delivery, a two-per-year frequency cap and 24-month lookback that would exclude most of 2024, a partial fix to the data use agreement that leaves its approved-purpose and aggregated-only clauses alive, a savings-clause qualifier for § 9.5, a Plan "acknowledgment" that the extract satisfies § 724, a release of Plan claims including indemnification, effectiveness conditioned on Continental's consent with a withdrawal right, year-only dates that cannot support the 100% audit, and no change to §§ 9.8/12.5. The rubric (45 criteria) also tests attestation mechanics (prior unqualified filings, the Additional Information field, and the attestation-period point even if the contract is fixed in December), IRC § 4980D exposure (employer liability, Form 8928, the (c)(3) reasonable-cause cap per year, the (c)(1)–(2) trigger-date analysis with the 30-day window closing about October 25, and the (b)(3) minimum tax on examination), the HIPAA structure of the data flow (safe-harbor dates, limited data set/BAA routes, plan-sponsor firewall), the lapsed non-renewal window and the changes-in-law trap, the Cordell-era data gap, the consultant's contingent transition fee and ERISA § 408(b)(2)(B) disclosure, and calibration criteria that penalise both signing the amendment as drafted and rejecting it wholesale. QA-flagged items were addressed: the September correspondence now post-dates the Northgate letter, the compound format criterion was split, and the c01/c05/c07/c20/c21 grader notes were tightened.
